mentions.snippet: On the max-cushion end, Hoka's Bondi 9 is the plushest shoe most testers have tried, and Runner's World named it a top pick for recovery days.
On makes the Cloudmonster, which feels bouncier but firmer underfoot; on the other hand, some runners find it harsh past 20 miles.
Brooks' Glycerin sits in the middle and is the safest choice if you're unsure. For most first-time marathoners I'd go with the Glycerin.
